stories.title: Status Yellow High Temperature warning issued for Ireland
stories.summary: A Status Yellow High Temperature warning has been issued for Ireland, with Met Éireann forecasting temperatures in excess of 27C in the coming days. The warning comes into place at 12pm tomorrow and will end at 9am on Friday. The forecaster warned of heat stress and uncomfortable sleeping conditions. It also said there may be water safety issues due to increased use of lakes and beaches.

stories.title: New retirement age rights to come into force next week
stories.summary: The Government has announced that new retirement age rights for employees will come into force from Monday 29 June. The legislation allows eligible workers to choose to remain in employment beyond their contractual retirement age, where that age is below the State pension age of 66. Currently, thousands of employees are forced to retire at the traditional retirement age of 65, as stated in their employment contracts, one year before the State pension commences. These new rules will give workers the option to work for an additional year to bridge that gap but there will be no requirement to do so.

stories.title: Writing was on wall as Britain set for 7th PM in 10 years
stories.summary: "In the last few days I've tried to persuade my colleagues that it would be eccentric to change governments... but as we’ve seen at Westminster the herd instinct is powerful and when the herd moves it moves, and no one is remotely indispensable." The words not of Keir Starmer outside Downing Street this morning as he announced he would be stepping down, but of Boris Johnson standing in exactly the same spot in July 2022 as he ended his premiership. That the words above could have been spoken by either man is an indication of how much has changed and how little has changed in a British political landscape that is now heading for its seventh Prime Minister in a decade. For a man who entered Number 10 almost exactly two years ago with a thumping overall majority and a promise to be different it transpires the end of his premiership was uncannily similar to his most recent predecessors.

stories.title: Cullen set to depart Leinster at end of next season
stories.summary: Leo Cullen will leave his role of head coach of Leinster Rugby at the end of next season. Cullen has been in charge of the province for over a decade and won a sixth URC title last Friday. He led them to European Cup success on one occasion, in 2018, but disappointingly has been unable to add to it since. They were defeated by Bordeaux Begles in the final of the latest edition at the end of May.

stories.title: Schools closed in parts of Europe as heatwave intensifies
stories.summary: Much of Europe was preparing today for an already fierce heatwave to intensify even further in the coming days, with some countries taking special measures to mitigate its effects. France recorded heat-related deaths over the weekend while a leading researcher reiterated that human-driven climate change had contributed to the recent record-breaking heatwave. In France, 49 of the country's 96 mainland departments were on a red alert weather warning, up from 35 over the weekend. Officials announced the closure of 845 schools today with another 1,800 schools set to let students leave earlier than normal.
